findings.title: Base, Pulse and Drive show unreadable status colours on the newly offered light suite themes
locations: ky_server_base web/src/styles/theme.css:32-43 (:root/patina --danger #ef4444, --success #10b981 are the only values for suite themes)
ky_server_base web/src/theme.ts:29 (data-theme=<suite id>; catalog palette sets no status colours by design)
KyDrive-server web/src/styles/theme.css:31-43 and web/src/theme.ts:26 (only --warning is adjusted for light themes)
findings.detail: These three products offered only Busnes plus the five base themes before this change. They now offer all 15 suite palettes with data-theme=<id>. No product block matches those ids and ky-ui deliberately leaves status colours to products (test/themes.test.js: 'suite palettes leave product status colours alone'). So --danger/--success fall back to Patina's dark-theme #ef4444/#10b981. KyCalendar and KyMessages close the same gap with a :not() tint rule (web/src/styles/theme.css:106); KyYard sets them inline by scheme. Affected text includes .dr-danger/.dr-ok, .dr-alert-error/.dr-alert-success, .app-logout and Drive alert icons and .btn-danger-quiet.
findings.evidence: status-contrast harness, min(contrast vs --panel, vs --bg): Base/Pulse/Drive light-matter danger 3.29 success 2.22; tropics 3.34/2.25; white-cliffs 3.57/2.40; sky 3.25/2.19; sun 3.42/2.31; polished-ky 3.35/2.25. Controls KyCalendar/KyMessages on the same themes: 9.34-10.91 danger, 7.70-9.51 success.
findings.fix: Port the KyCalendar/KyMessages rule (theme.css:106-110) into each product's styles/theme.css, adding --warning for Base/Pulse and replacing Drive's inline --warning special case. Alternatively, set the colours inline by scheme as KyYard does.
findings.verification: node /tmp/claude-fleet-review/status-contrast.mjs (source in runtime-source-review.md appendix B). Today: Base/Pulse/Drive rows < 4.5. After the fix every light-theme danger/success value is >= 4.5, as the Calendar and Messages rows already are.

findings.title: KyDNS and KyRecovery no longer guarantee the saved theme before first paint
locations: kydns-server internal/web/templates/base.html:14-15 (classic head scripts replaced by modulepreload + type=module)
findings.detail: Before the change, a synchronous classic head script applied the saved choice before the body was parsed. The old KyDNS theme.js comment states this purpose. Module scripts are deferred and not render-blocking. If the module fetch is slower than first paint, the OS-following Busnes default paints first. That covers both named themes and explicit Busnes Light/Dark choices opposite the OS. KyDNS is a multi-page app, so the race recurs on every navigation. ky-ui AGENTS explicitly says deferred modules make no first-paint promise, so the shared contract tolerates this. These two products, however, previously made that promise. The implementer note marked this as unproven.
findings.evidence: first-paint harness, theme script delayed 800 ms. Base revisions applied the theme before first contentful paint (DNS Ocean: applied 887 ms, FCP 920 ms; Recovery light on OS dark: applied 853 ms, FCP 944 ms). Head revisions painted first (DNS Ocean FCP 68 ms, applied 843 ms; DNS 'Busnes Light' on OS dark FCP 76/839; Recovery 'light' on OS dark FCP 132/862; Recovery 'ocean' FCP 104/850). With no delay on loopback, 0 of 12 head runs flashed. This is a timing race, not a deterministic flash.
findings.fix: Restore a small synchronous classic bootstrap in <head> that reads the key and applies data-theme plus the palette before paint. For example, have sync-consumers generate a classic themes-browser.js global, as palettes-browser.js was, and keep the module for the picker. Minimum mitigation: add blocking="render" to the module script. Chromium honours it; other engines keep today's behaviour.
findings.verification: node /tmp/claude-fleet-review/first-paint.mjs (appendix A). Old revisions print paintedBeforeSavedTheme=false and heads print true. After the fix, the head rows print false.

findings.title: Pre-existing: light named themes on a dark OS get Busnes Dark status colours in products that remove data-theme
locations: ky-ui src/tokens.css:91-110 (alias block :root:not([data-theme]):not([data-ky-theme]) sets --danger/--success/--warning/--ink-muted from OS-following --ky-* at specificity 0,3,0)
KyIdentity-server web/src/theme.ts:15 (named theme deletes data-theme), and the same pattern in KyNotes, KyPost and KyDNS theme.js
findings.detail: Measured in KyIdentity: identical at the base and head revisions, so this change did not cause it. It is reported because the brief asks for status contrast. The new base-family themes (paper and others) set their own status colours inline, so they are not affected. KyRecovery avoids the problem by keeping data-theme=busnes-<scheme> under named palettes.
findings.evidence: status-contrast harness, KyIdentity with OS dark, light suite themes: danger 2.10-2.30, success 1.78-1.95, at both ba43fbe9 and cf986204.
findings.fix: Separate follow-up. Have these adapters keep a scheme-matched data-ky-theme for named palettes, as KyRecovery does, or set status colours inline by scheme.
findings.verification: status-contrast harness 'KyIdentity head, OS dark' row reaches >= 4.5.

findings.title: KyIdentity and KyNotes Appearance radios do not follow another tab's choice
findings.detail: watchChoice re-applies the theme, but the component state is read once. The checked radio stays on the old theme after a change in another tab. Clicking that stale-checked card produces no change event, so the user must pick a different card first. Every other product updates its radios through storage, ky:theme or useSyncExternalStore. The old swatch and select UIs had the same staleness.
findings.evidence: Source reasoning only (React-controlled radio); not executed.
findings.fix: Add the same storage listener KyCalendar uses (pages/Appearance.tsx:8-12).
findings.verification: Two tabs on Appearance: choose Sun in tab B, then Ocean must appear checked in tab A without a reload.

findings.title: Spec question: KyYard and KyNotes reach Appearance through Settings, not a primary-navigation link
locations: KyYard-Server web/src/components/AppHeader.tsx:13-15 and web/src/pages/Settings.tsx:11-14 (Appearance is the default Settings tab for every role)
findings.detail: The other nine web interfaces add an 'Appearance' primary-nav item for every signed-in role. KyYard and KyNotes keep the pre-existing Settings -> Appearance placement. It is reachable for every role in one or two steps, and the compact dropdown is gone. The owner rule reads 'keep an Appearance navigation link'. Whether Settings placement satisfies it is the owner's call, not a code defect.
findings.fix: Ask the owner. If a primary link is required, add /settings?section=appearance (KyYard) or an Appearance nav entry that opens Settings at #appearance (KyNotes).

findings.title: Phone horizontal navigation does not reveal the current item (Base, Pulse, Drive, Recovery)
findings.detail: Appearance is now the last item. On a 390 px reload of Pulse's #/appearance, the selected item can sit off-screen, with no visible scrollbar on Recovery. It stays operable by swipe and by keyboard focus, which scrolls into view. KyMessages scrolls the current item into view (AppHeader.tsx:41). This is shell consistency, not a reachability failure.
findings.fix: Reuse KyMessages' scrollIntoView({inline:'nearest'}) on route change.
findings.verification: 390x844, open Appearance, reload: the selected nav item intersects the viewport.

findings.title: Implementer notes checked
findings.detail: KyYard: LOCAL_PALETTE keeps Polished Ky --button-text #021716 (theme.ts:11, 29), which measures 5.04:1 on #0891b2. The catalog #042f2e measures 3.93:1 and is inherited by the other products; that is the stated acceptance gap. KyDrive: the five base themes skip inline catalog colours, and previews read the product's own [data-theme] blocks (theme.css:71-77), so rendered colours and saved IDs are preserved; paper differs from the catalog by design. KyRecovery: --ink is scoped to the picker; navigation.css and appearance.css read no surface from --ink; status colours follow the palette's scheme via data-theme=busnes-<scheme>; no collision found. Calendar/Messages global hover fix (button:not(:where(.ky-nav-item))) and the KyPost reader are untouched. Vendored ky-ui files in all 11 consumers are byte-identical to ab7a039, and generated palettes and VERSION are identical across consumers. Legacy base-theme CSS in Calendar, Messages, Yard, Base and Pulse equals THEME_PALETTES; Drive paper differs and is handled. Login-page selects (Calendar, Messages, Base, Pulse, Drive), Drive's admin Settings select, KyPost's admin ApplicationRuntime select (no Match system option, pre-existing) and the KyRecovery ceremony select are outside navigation and allowed by the owner correction. ky-server-base Dashboard dropped its 'Verified Ready' claim, a copy change in the safe direction.

limits: Source audit only; no visual acceptance or screenshot scoring.
Product test suites were not rerun; implementer-reported passes are not re-certified here.
Harnesses use real committed CSS/JS but synthetic pages, not full product builds.
F4 and F6 are reasoned from source and not executed.
